clue.text: Shot after warning shout to give up

indicators.note: the attempt word is placed after the shout in the answer

parts.note: golfers shout 'fore' to warn others of an incoming ball
a shot is a go, an attempt

explanation.surface: A sharp cry of alarm rings out just before someone surrenders.
explanation.definitionFit: To forego something is to do without it, which is to relinquish or abandon it.

clue.text: Quick to accommodate soldiers with space in part of ship

indicators.note: to accommodate is to house, so the quick word holds the others inside it

parts.note: quick means fast
OR, other ranks, are ordinary soldiers
an em is a printer's unit of space

explanation.surface: A speedy rearrangement of a vessel makes room for troops.
explanation.definitionFit: The foremast is the mast nearest the bow of a sailing vessel.

clue.text: Racket hobo created around town to cause a disturbance

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the abbreviation for town
created suggests the letters are made into something new, a rearrangement

parts.note: T is a standard abbreviation for town

explanation.surface: A noisy tramp makes trouble in the streets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Racket' and 'hobo' look like the scene's noise and vagrant, but they are just the letters to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To rock the boat is an idiom for upsetting a settled situation and stirring up trouble.

clue.text: Yield under pressure from Grant

definitions.meaning: a material that ... bends or sags when pressed

explanation.surface: Someone caves in when a person called Grant leans on them.
explanation.definitionFit: Give is both the flex of a material under load and the act of bestowing something.

clue.text: Worried? Trust me to bag leading part in Working Girl

indicators.note: to bag is to capture, so the rearranged letters enclose the next piece
worried letters are fretted and disturbed into a new order
the leading letter of the word part is the one taken

explanation.surface: An anxious actor tells a director to trust them with the lead in the film Working Girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried' shuffles TRUST ME; 'to bag' puts P, the 'leading' letter of 'part', inside. Working Girl is also a 1988 film title.
explanation.definitionFit: Strumpet is an old pejorative for a prostitute, euphemistically called a working girl.

clue.text: Feature of stage trickery associated with nameless benefactor

parts.note: a trap is a piece of trickery

indicators.note: N abbreviates name, so nameless means that letter is dropped

parts.note: a donor is a benefactor

explanation.surface: Theatrical sleight of hand is linked to an anonymous patron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nameless' removes N from DONOR, leaving DOOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapdoor in the floor of a theatre lets actors appear or vanish.

clue.text: Implied when lower in rank than Rose

parts.note: someone lower in rank is under another
rose, as in got to one's feet, gives stood

explanation.surface: Someone is hinted to rank below a woman called Rose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a name or a flower but is the past tense of rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Something understood is taken as agreed without being stated, which is tacit or implicit.

clue.text: God of sleep sent up

indicators.note: in a down entry, sent up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: A deity of slumber is mocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' turns NAP upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Pan is the Greek god of shepherds and wild places.

clue.text: Obliged to store pears evenly in rows

indicators.note: to store is to keep inside, so the first word holds the picked letters

parts.note: obliged, bound by duty, means tied

indicators.note: evenly picks the even-numbered letters of the following word

explanation.surface: A greengrocer is required to lay out the fruit in neat lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evenly' takes E and R, the 2nd and 4th letters of 'pears', and 'to store' puts them inside TIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiered describes something arranged in successive rising levels or ranks.

clue.text: Bear seen in stream

explanation.surface: A bear is spotted in a watercourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Brook is a verb for tolerating and a noun for a small flowing creek.

clue.text: Get better insurance after a couple of reminders

indicators.note: the insurance word comes after the picked letters
a couple of means the first two letters of the next word are taken

parts.note: insurance is cover

explanation.surface: Someone upgrades their policy after a couple of renewal notices.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover is to regain health after an illness.

clue.text: Moderately slow start to novel by a writer from Italy

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: Dante Alighieri was the Italian poet of the Divine Comedy

explanation.surface: An Italian author makes a leisurely beginning to a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Andante is the musical tempo marking for a walking, moderately slow pace.

clue.text: Very small amount of exactly what is needed discovered in Maine

indicators.note: something discovered in a place is found inside it

parts.note: ME is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Maine
'it' is the very thing, exactly what is wanted

explanation.surface: A tiny quantity of the perfect thing turns up in a New England state.
explanation.definitionFit: A mite is a tiny bit, as in the widow's mite.

clue.text: Former Aussie skipper has story about Bradman's last boundary

parts.note: Allan Border captained Australia's cricket team

indicators.note: about means the fib goes around the picked letter

parts.note: a story can be a lie

indicators.note: the last letter of Bradman is taken

explanation.surface: A cricket captain tells a tale about Don Bradman's final hit to the rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts N, the 'last' letter of Bradman, inside LIE. Allan Border and Don Bradman were both Australian cricket captains; a boundary is a hit to the edge of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: A borderline is the dividing line between two areas.

clue.text: Surprisingly intent on supporting current Conservative leader lacking in self- restraint

indicators.note: in a down entry the supporting piece sits below the others

parts.note: current, as in fashionable, means in

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
surprisingly hints the letters turn out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A Tory chief, determined to back the present line, seems unable to control himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Surprisingly' shuffles INTENT into TINENT, which 'supporting' places beneath IN, C and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Incontinent means unable to hold back one's urges or emotions.

clue.text: Harsh criticism of drug taking in Romania's capital after short investigation

indicators.note: taking in means the drug word holds the following pieces

parts.note: opium is a narcotic drug

indicators.note: the Romanian letter comes after the shortened inquiry
short means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a probe is an investigation

indicators.note: the capital of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A brief inquiry into narcotics in Bucharest draws heavy censure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims the inquiry word, the capital letter of Romania follows it, and 'taking in' places both inside the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Opprobrium is public disgrace or scornful condemnation.

clue.text: Record on favourites coming from behind is plain

indicators.note: coming from behind means the letters are read from the end backwards

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
pets are favourites

explanation.surface: A disc featuring the favourites charges late to win, which is clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming from behind' reads EPPETS backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A steppe is a vast treeless grassland, as in Central Asia.

clue.text: Touch on meeting Tom back in court

indicators.note: the pieces are placed within the court abbreviation
back means the word is turned round

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

explanation.surface: A meeting with Tom back in court is touched upon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CAT to TAC; ON and TAC go 'in' CT.
explanation.definitionFit: Contact is physical touching, or communication with someone.

clue.text: Periodical on literature primarily occupying eccentric dean of an Oxford college

parts.note: a mag, short for magazine, is a periodical

indicators.note: the picked letter occupies the space inside the jumbled letters
eccentric means off-centre, so the letters are jumbled
primarily picks the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: An odd Oxford dean is absorbed in a literary magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' shuffles DEAN, and 'occupying' puts L, the 'primarily' letter of 'literature', inside to give DALEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Magdalen, pronounced 'maudlin', is one of the colleges of the University of Oxford.

clue.text: Be noncommittal when school chum of Copperfield ultimately gets to the top

indicators.note: the final letter climbs to the head of the down entry

parts.note: Tommy Traddles is David Copperfield's schoolfriend in Dickens's novel

explanation.surface: A Dickens character finally rises to the top while refusing to commit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately gets to the top' moves the last letter, S, of TRADDLES to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To straddle an issue is to sit on the fence, favouring neither side.

clue.text: Complaints essentially stopping needy women's means of support

indicators.note: stopping means plugging a gap, so the picked letters go inside

parts.note: the needy are poor
W abbreviates women

indicators.note: essentially picks the central letters, the essence, of the word

explanation.surface: Grievances at heart end support for hard-up women.
explanation.walkthrough: The Poor Law was the old English system of relief for the destitute, administered by parishes.
explanation.definitionFit: The Poor Law provided public relief, a safety net for paupers.

clue.text: Toff taken aback by ultimate in headgear

indicators.note: aback means backwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: a nob is a toff, a posh person
net means final, as in the net result

explanation.surface: A posh gent is startled by the last word in hats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' looks like surprise but reverses NOB.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonnet is a hat tied under the chin.

clue.text: Look sullen over idle talk dismissing German's work

indicators.note: the scowl word goes over, covering, the shortened chatter

parts.note: to lour is to scowl or look sullen

indicators.note: dismissing means the letter is sent away

parts.note: gab is idle chatter
G abbreviates German

explanation.surface: Someone scowls at a German's work while dismissing chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' here means covering: the scowl word wraps round what is left once 'dismissing' sends the German letter away.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour is toil, physical or mental effort.

clue.text: Red line crossed by us? On the contrary

indicators.note: one piece is crossed, cut through, by the other
on the contrary reverses roles, so the line is cut by us rather than the reverse

parts.note: a ley is a line, as in ley lines
us is the Financial Times, which publishes the puzzle

explanation.surface: A red line is breached by the newspaper, or rather the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips 'line crossed by us', so us goes inside the line. 'Us' is the Financial Times, which sets this puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A lefty is a left-winger, and red is slang for a socialist or communist.

clue.text: Obtains print-out including break down of bacterium deactivators

indicators.note: the jumbled letters include the next piece inside them
the 'out' in print-out suggests the letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: a machine that breaks down dies

explanation.surface: A lab gets a printout that includes the breakdown of germ killers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'print-out' shuffles the letters of 'Obtains' into ANTIBOS, and 'including' puts the dying word inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Antibodies are blood proteins that neutralise invading microbes.

clue.text: Privileged Ivanka's not entirely a prima donna

indicators.note: not entirely means only part of the words is used, a run found inside them

explanation.surface: Pampered Ivanka Trump is something of a demanding star.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside 'privilegeD IVAnka'.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated female opera singer, or a temperamental star.

clue.text: A helpful piece of advice about making bread

indicators.note: about means the letters are turned around

parts.note: a tip is a helpful hint

explanation.surface: A baker offers a useful hint about making a loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns A TIP round.
explanation.definitionFit: Pita is a flat Middle Eastern bread, also spelt pitta.

clue.text: Familiar weapon of the police

parts.note: old, as in old friend, means familiar
a bill is a long-handled bladed weapon

explanation.surface: A well-known police weapon, such as a truncheon.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Bill is British slang for the police force.

clue.text: Useless bit of pseudo-galena

definitions.note: the adjective stands for the noun sense of something worthless

indicators.note: bit of means only a fragment of the following word is used

explanation.surface: A sample of fake lead ore is worthless.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside 'pseuDO-Galena'. Galena is lead ore.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog is slang for a hopeless, inferior thing, as in 'this car is a dog'.

clue.text: The final part of story spoken in French by Penny

indicators.note: spoken signals a word said aloud for its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a tale is a story
en is French for in
D, from denarius, was the old British penny

explanation.surface: A storyteller relates the ending in French to someone called Penny.
explanation.definitionFit: The tail end is the very last portion of something.

clue.text: Organise books on administration

indicators.note: in an across clue, books on administration puts the books after it

parts.note: a regime is a government or administration
NT, New Testament, is a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A government's records are put in order.
explanation.definitionFit: To regiment is to impose strict order or discipline on people.

clue.text: Conflict in Britain — PM finally resigns

indicators.note: the final letter steps down and is removed

parts.note: Clement Attlee was British Prime Minister 1945 to 1951

explanation.surface: Political strife in the UK ends with the Prime Minister quitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally resigns' drops ATTLEE's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A battle is a fight between opposing forces.
